title: Runs agree under an embedding on guarded states
statement: Let the source and host be multi-tape Turing machines with $k$ work tapes, a common symbol alphabet, and state sets $S$ and $H$, and let $x$ be an input word. Let $e:S\hookrightarrow H$ be an injective map and let $G$ be a predicate on source states. Suppose that, for every $q\in S$ satisfying $G(q)$ and every scanned input symbol and tuple of work-tape symbols, the host transition at $e(q)$ equals the source transition at $q$ with its successor state mapped by $e$. For any source configuration $c$ on $x$ and any $t\in\mathbb{N}$, if at every time $u<t$ the run of the source machine from $c$ has state $q$ only when $G(q)$ holds, then running the host for $t$ steps from the configuration obtained by mapping the state of $c$ along $e$ yields the configuration reached by the source after $t$ steps, with its state mapped along $e$.
hypotheses_covered: Source and host machines with $k$ work tapes and a common symbol alphabet
Transition agreement after state mapping at every state satisfying $G$, for all scanned symbols
A source configuration $c$ and natural-number time $t$
At every time $u<t$, any present source-run state satisfies $G$
